metadata.research_goal: Create backend-ready cycling records for learn-to-ride, general fitness, commuting, indoor cycling, older adults, habit formation, beginner safety, and conservative progression.
metadata.write_scope: single draft file for beginner, fitness, commuter, indoor, and accessible cycling contexts
metadata.synthesis_note: Records prioritize progression, safety, accessibility, and backend plan adjustments rather than race-performance programming.

key_concepts.concept: Beginner cycling is a safety, handling, confidence, and aerobic-habit problem, not only an endurance problem.
key_concepts.backend_use: Beginner plans should include handling drills, short easy rides, route choice, bike checks, and recovery before hard intervals.

key_concepts.concept: Confidence in starting, stopping, turning, braking, looking, and shifting should come before speed, traffic complexity, or group riding.
key_concepts.backend_use: Block high-speed descents, fast group rides, and maximal sprints until handling readiness is marked true.

key_concepts.concept: Commuting creates frequent low-to-moderate exposure that can build fitness but also accumulates fatigue and contact-point irritation.
key_concepts.backend_use: Count commute rides in weekly load and protect recovery when commute volume rises.

key_concepts.concept: Indoor cycling removes traffic and handling demands but increases monotony, heat stress, fixed-position time, and saddle/contact-point load.
key_concepts.backend_use: Indoor plans need ventilation, hydration, position changes, and progressive duration even when fitness feels ready.

key_concepts.concept: Cycling is low impact but high repetition, so beginners can still develop knee, saddle, hand, neck, or low-back symptoms.
key_concepts.backend_use: Do not progress duration or intensity when contact-point pain or joint pain worsens.

key_concepts.concept: Cycling can help users reach weekly aerobic activity targets, but strength work should still support major muscle groups and posture.
key_concepts.backend_use: Fitness cycling plans should include two weekly strength or mobility-support sessions when possible.

key_concepts.concept: Route difficulty is a training variable: traffic, turns, hills, surface, weather, lighting, and stop-start density change session demand.
key_concepts.backend_use: Store route context and reduce planned intensity when the route already contains hills, traffic stress, or technical handling.

key_concepts.concept: Most short beginner rides need simple hydration and normal meals, but longer rides need planned fluids and carbohydrate availability.
key_concepts.backend_use: Trigger fueling guidance when ride duration exceeds 60-75 minutes or when heat, hills, or low energy are reported.

technical_models.name: Beginner cycling control ladder
technical_models.progression_signal: Advance only when the rider can start, stop, brake, turn, and scan without panic or wobbling.

technical_models.name: Safe commute progression ladder
technical_models.progression_signal: Advance when route navigation and traffic behavior are predictable without elevated stress.

technical_models.name: Beginner fitness duration ladder
technical_models.progression_signal: Increase duration only when next-day knee, saddle, hand, neck, and low-back response is stable.

technical_models.name: Indoor beginner cycling session model
avoid: high heat without fan or fluids

technical_models.name: Commute load accounting model
technical_models.backend_use: Treat commuting as training volume, especially when the user rides both directions or carries load.

technical_models.name: Older adult accessible cycling model
technical_models.backend_use: Prefer stable, low-risk environments and gradual time progression when balance, joint pain, or confidence is limited.

technical_models.name: Beginner RPE model
targets: short harder efforts only after base and safety
technical_models.backend_use: Use RPE and talk-test language before power zones for most new riders.

technical_models.name: Basic pre-ride bike check
technical_models.backend_use: Include as a recurring beginner safety task before outdoor rides.

tactical_rules.rule: New riders should first learn control skills away from traffic before progressing to quiet roads and then busier environments.
If a beginner route has traffic, hills, poor surface, night riding, or bad weather, do not also prescribe hard intensity.
Commuting rides count toward weekly aerobic and fatigue load even when the user does not label them workouts.
Fast group rides should wait until the user can ride predictably, brake smoothly, hold line, signal, and manage proximity.
Indoor rides longer than 30 minutes should include ventilation and hydration prompts because heat buildup increases perceived effort.
For beginner fitness riders, hills should be treated as intensity even if the planned session says easy.
Do not increase ride duration when saddle, hand, neck, knee, or low-back discomfort worsens after recent rides.
For weight-loss users, use repeatable moderate rides and strength support instead of exhausting punishment rides that disrupt consistency.
Low-light, night, rain, or traffic-heavy commutes require visibility, route, and safety prompts before performance goals.
tactical_rules.backend_trigger: commute_context includes low_light OR rain OR high_traffic

tactical_rules.rule: Beginner easy rides should remain conversational; if the user cannot talk in short sentences, reduce resistance, gear, hill exposure, or pace.

physical_demands.backend_use: Increase frequency and duration before hard intensity.

physical_demands.beginner_expression: saddle, hand, neck, and back comfort during and after rides
smooth stop without panic or skid
pedal smoothly without grinding heavy gears
physical_demands.backend_use: Reduce knee stress and improve ride economy.

physical_demands.beginner_expression: hold relaxed position without neck/hand overload
look ahead, signal, notice hazards, and maintain line
repeat low-to-moderate pedal force without knee irritation
physical_demands.backend_use: Progress duration and mild hills conservatively.

injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Hold duration, suggest fit/contact review, and break long rides into shorter blocks.
Add posture cues, upper-back support, grip changes, and fit review.
Reduce duration, choose upright setup, add trunk/hip mobility and strength support.

injury_or_load_risks.risk: knee discomfort from heavy gear grinding
injury_or_load_risks.backend_adjustment: Use easier gears, reduce hills, keep cadence comfortable, and flag fit review if persistent.
Use lower-intensity route practice and avoid performance goals that day.
Prompt fan/fluids and lower intensity if RPE drifts above target.
Reduce added training intensity and count commute rides in weekly load.
Require skill progression and safe environment before speed or complexity.

training_implications.implication: For new riders, two to four short easy rides per week is usually better than one long exhausting ride.
training_implications.backend_use: Prioritize frequency and confidence before long-ride build.

training_implications.implication: RPE and talk test are more useful than FTP for true beginners.
training_implications.backend_use: Do not require power zones during onboarding.

training_implications.implication: General fitness cyclists still need strength and mobility support for posture, hips, trunk, and major muscle groups.
training_implications.backend_use: Pair cycling with simple S&C sessions when schedule allows.

training_implications.implication: A user commuting four to ten rides per week may already have significant aerobic load.
training_implications.backend_use: Auto-adjust hard sessions downward when commute load is high.

training_implications.implication: Hills should be introduced gradually after flat-route control and easy ride tolerance.
training_implications.backend_use: Use hill exposure as a progression, not a default.

training_implications.implication: Indoor beginners may tolerate cardiovascular load before contact points are ready.
training_implications.backend_use: Progress indoor duration slowly and include position changes.

training_implications.implication: For beginners and commuters, a session can legitimately target braking, route practice, or signaling rather than fitness.
training_implications.backend_use: Allow cycling skill sessions in program output.

training_implications.implication: Fitness and weight-loss users need repeatable energy expenditure, not aggressive interval density.
training_implications.backend_use: Use easy/moderate rides, gradual duration, and recovery consistency.

training_implications.implication: Older adults or users with balance concerns may need stationary/recumbent bikes or protected paths first.
training_implications.backend_use: Match cycling mode to balance, confidence, and joint history.

training_implications.implication: Fueling guidance becomes more important as ride duration passes 60-75 minutes or heat/hills increase.
training_implications.backend_use: Trigger simple pre-ride and on-ride fueling prompts.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling beginner control ladder
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Bike check, mount/dismount, start/stop, straight-line ride, braking, wide turns, look/signal, shifting, quiet-route ride.

backend_records_to_create.name: Beginner cycling easy-ride rule
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Use conversational RPE, short duration, flat safe routes, and next-day symptom checks before progressing.

backend_records_to_create.name: Commute rides count as training load
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Add commute duration/frequency/hills/traffic stress to weekly load and reduce extra intervals when commute load is high.

backend_records_to_create.name: Indoor beginner cycling setup
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Include fan, fluids, easy warmup, progressive duration, position changes, and no maximal work for low-readiness users.

backend_records_to_create.name: Beginner contact-point pain hold
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Hold ride duration progression when saddle, hand, neck, or low-back discomfort worsens.

backend_records_to_create.name: Beginner road readiness
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Can start, stop, brake, turn, scan, signal, shift, and hold line calmly in low-complexity settings.

backend_records_to_create.name: Cycling for general health baseline
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Build toward public-health aerobic activity targets while preserving two weekly strength-support opportunities when possible.

backend_records_to_create.name: Route complexity modifies intensity
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: High traffic, poor visibility, hills, rain, or unfamiliar routes reduce or replace planned intensity.

backend_records_to_create.name: Fitness cycling profile
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: General aerobic health, weight loss, low-impact conditioning, habit formation, progressive duration, and basic strength support.

backend_records_to_create.name: Commuter cycling profile
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Frequent practical rides, route/safety demands, hidden training load, weather/visibility factors, and equipment practicality.

backend_records_to_create.name: Beginner cycling confidence foundation
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Four-week pattern: control skills, short easy rides, flat-route exposure, route planning, and contact-point monitoring.

backend_records_to_create.name: Beginner no fast group ride gate
backend_records_to_create.payload_seed: Block fast group riding until line-holding, smooth braking, signaling, proximity comfort, and route awareness are stable.
